Sam (Support): FYI - Astraeus opened an escalation: consistent 429s and high token latency from their dedicated pool during nightly batch windows. Starting this thread to triage and propose an action plan. (root: 1778529630)

Astraeus Ops: Confirming. Between ~02:00-03:30 UTC last night we saw short spikes up to ~420 QPS for 2-4m, baseline steady-state ~28 QPS. Pool is currently 3xA100-80G reserved. 429 rate during burst window ~12%, overall errors spike; p95 token latency climbed to ~2.8s. Auth failures: small (~0.4%) but visible during the same window.

Sam (Support): Thanks — I pulled the pool telemetry and trace samples. Quick summary: GPU utilization hovered ~95-99% during bursts, queue depth spiked, request queueing visible in runtime logs. No account-level rate limit triggered; these are pool-level throttles.

Lee (SRE): Metrics excerpt from 02:00-03:15 UTC: ```{\n  \"time_range\": \"02:00-03:15\",\n  \"peak_qps\": 420,\n  \"baseline_qps\": 28,\n  \"gpu_utilization_avg\": 0.96,\n  \"gpu_utilization_peak\": 0.99,\n  \"p50_latency_ms\": 620,\n  \"p95_latency_ms\": 2800,\n  \"429_rate\": 0.12\n}```This looks like classic undersized pool for a short, high-concurrency batch spike.

Astraeus Ops: We observed the job is a set of parallel inference requests kicked off by their analytics pipeline. They prefer not to change job structure. They need guidance on sizing and short-term mitigations.

Maya (Customer Success): Priority: get them stable for tonight's window and provide a sizing recommendation + approximate cost.

Sam (Support): Immediate mitigations we can take tonight (quick wins):
- Temporarily increase pool capacity from 3 -> 6 GPUs for tonight's window.
- Add a pre-warm schedule to provision extra instances at 01:45 UTC for 30m.
- Adjust autoscale policy: min=3, max=8, scale_up.cooldown=60s, target_utilization=0.6.
- Enable request-level queuing telemetry to confirm the queue drains after scaling.

Lee (SRE): Quick calc for longer-term sizing: current sustained peak util ~0.96 on 3 GPUs. To target 60% utilization at peak: required_gpus = (current_util * current_gpus) / target_util = (0.96 * 3)/0.6 ≈ 4.8 -> round up to 5. Recommend 6 GPUs to give ~20% headroom for traffic variability and parallelism.

Sam (Support): Also recommend pre-warming KV cache / model sharded states. Run warmup queries that exercise typical prefix lengths and batch sizes so kernels are JIT'd and caches hot. Example warmup curl snippet:
```bash
# run from CI runner ~15m before window
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n    -d '{"model":"open-gpt-13b","input":"warmup query '"$i"'","max_tokens":64}' &
done
wait
```
This will create steady load to spin up kernels and prime KV caches.

Astraeus Ops: If we scale to 6 tonight, please also include a simple smoke check post-warmup so we can confirm p95 falls under 1s.

Sam (Support): Agreed. Plan for tonight:
1) Increase pool to 6 GPUs at 01:40 UTC.
2) Run warmup job at 01:45 UTC for 15-30m.
3) Monitor p95, 429 rate, and GPU util closely; rollback scale-down only after metrics stable for 20m.
4) Share post-window telemetry and a short report.

autoscale-bot: autoscale.change.requested {\"pool_id\":\"astraeus-prod-1\",\"from\":3,\"to\":6,\"requested_by\":\"Sam (Support)\",\"status\":\"pending\"}

Lee (SRE): Noisy-neighbor check: I scanned per-tenant connection and long-lived stream counts during the window. One tenant (internal_test_tenant) shows ~4x more concurrent open streams during the batch. That could exacerbate queueing. Recommend isolating or throttling that tenant if observed again.

Maya (Customer Success): Cost/estimate question from Astraeus: what is the approximate incremental cost of going 3 -> 6 GPUs?

Sam (Support): Rough monthly delta estimate for reserved A100-equivalent capacity (ballpark): ~$6,000 per GPU/month * 3 additional GPUs = ~$18k/mo. If they only need scaling for nightly window we can do scheduled burst (no full reservation) which is cheaper short-term; engineering/finance can refine.

Astraeus Ops: We approve the temporary increase tonight. Please proceed and share the post-window report + a recommended long-term configuration (scheduled warm-up + headroom policy). Also we want a runbook to avoid repeating this.

Lee (SRE): I'll open an internal action item: ENG-INC-4132 - \"Astraeus dedicated pool right-sizing + warmup runbook\" assigned to eng-oncall. Will include: exact autoscale policy snippet, warmup script, smoke checks, and cost estimate.

Sam (Support): One more note — if they expect more frequent big batch bursts, consider changing the client-side pattern: shard/retry with jitter or smoothing the launch window. If they can't change the producer, we'll recommend permanent higher min-capacity or a scheduled burst product.

Astraeus Ops: Thanks all. We'll watch tonight and post results here. Appreciate quick response. :thumbsup:

Sam (Support): Thanks — will update after rollout and attach telemetry. :white_check_mark:
